Shedeur
SHED-ee-ur
proper noun
Hebrew Shedeyur (H7707), commonly read as caster forth of light or the Almighty is light — joining Shaddai (H7706), the Almighty, to ur (H217), flame or light.

Biblical Definition

Shedeur is known to Scripture only as a father. Five times the wilderness record names him, and every time in the same construction: Elizur the son of Shedeur (Num 1:5; 2:10; 7:30, 35; 10:18). He is of the tribe of Reuben, and he never speaks, acts, or is numbered in his own right. That is worth pausing over. The generation that came out of Egypt fell in the wilderness for unbelief (Heb 3:17-19), and Shedeur was of that generation; the son stands at the head of the tribe while the father's whole record is the single word son of. Yet the record is not nothing. Israel reckoned every prince by his father's house — heads of the house of their fathers (Num 7:2) — and a man whose name is attached to the captain of Reuben in four separate chapters has left a real mark on the covenant people. The name itself carries light: Shaddai is light. Set beside his son's name, my God is a rock, the pair reads as a household confession handed down — light from the father, refuge from the son. Israelite naming was catechesis, and a family that named its sons this way was teaching the next generation who God is before that generation could speak.

Origin & Era

A Reubenite of the wilderness generation, father of Elizur the prince of Reuben; his name signifies light from the Almighty.

SHEDEUR, Hebrew Shedeyur, caster forth of light, or the Almighty is light.

A man of the tribe of Reuben in the generation that came out of Egypt.

Father of Elizur, prince and captain of the children of Reuben.

Named five times in the book of Numbers, always as the father of Elizur.

Nothing else of his life is recorded in Scripture.

Key Scripture

Num 1:5 — "And these are the names of the men that shall stand with you: of the tribe of Reuben; Elizur the son of Shedeur."

Num 7:30 — "On the fourth day Elizur the son of Shedeur, prince of the children of Reuben, did offer:"

Num 7:35 — "And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this was the offering of Elizur the son of Shedeur."

Num 2:10 — "On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben according to their armies: and the captain of the children of Reuben shall be Elizur the son of Shedeur."

Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that fatherhood is a real office whose fruit outlives the record of the father.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. No movement has any interest in Shedeur. What presses on a modern reader instead is the smallness of the record — a man remembered only as somebody's father — and the instinct to count that a waste. Our age measures a life by what it accomplishes under its own name, and a man whose entire scriptural footprint is the phrase son of Shedeur looks, by that measure, like nothing at all.

Scripture measures otherwise. The command to fathers is to teach the words of God diligently unto their children, talking of them when they sit in the house and when they walk by the way (Deu 6:7), and the fruit of that work usually appears under another man's name. Shedeur raised a son whom the LORD named to stand beside Moses. Timothy's faith dwelt first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2Ti 1:5), and it is Timothy's name on the epistle. The principle to recover is that the ordinary, unrecorded labour of a godly household is not a lesser kind of service; it is the ordinary means by which God supplies the next generation's leaders.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Shedeyur (H7707), from Shaddai (H7706), the Almighty, and ur (H217), flame, light — light from the Almighty.

expand to see more

Hebrew Shedeyur (H7707) — the Reubenite father of Elizur; Numbers 1:5, 2:10, 7:30, 7:35, 10:18.

Hebrew Shaddai (H7706) — the Almighty, the covenant name by which God appeared to the patriarchs (Exo 6:3).

Hebrew ur (H217) — flame, light; the same root behind the Urim of the high priest's breastplate.

Hebrew ben (H1121) — son; the word that carries Shedeur's entire biblical record, Elizur the son of Shedeur.

Hebrew ab (H1) — father; Israel reckoned her princes by the house of their fathers, Numbers 7:2.

Usage

"“Elizur the son of Shedeur” — the whole of his record, repeated five times."

"“This was the offering of Elizur the son of Shedeur”."

"“Heads of the house of their fathers, who were the princes of the tribes” (Num 7:2)."
